prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-05-07, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-05-07):
| Current ratio           | 0.99 |
| Retained earnings       | 13,060M |
| Current liabilities     | 6,096M |
| Current assets          | 6,043M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 10,004M |
| Total liabilities       | 15,009M |
| Total assets            | 25,041M |
| EBIT / operating income | 622M |
| Revenue                 | 4,066M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows a near-break-even liquidity position (current ratio ~0.99) with solid profitability (EBIT 622M on 4,066M revenue) and a strong equity base (retained earnings 13,060M, shareholders' equity 10,004M). However, leverage is elevated (total liabilities 15,009M vs. assets 25,041M) and liquidity is marginal, suggesting some refinancing or liquidity risk if cash flow falters. Overall, credit risk appears modest but not premium, supporting a mid-investment-grade rating.

DECISION: BBB
